name: Harriet Hageman

issue_poll.name: Cygnal for Keep It Public Wyoming, Wyoming Republican primary voters (n=400+), late July 2026 - most important issue; plus New Bridge Strategy for Natrona Collective Health Trust, Wyoming registered voters (n=545), Feb 10-16, 2026 - share calling each an extremely/very serious problem; plus Colorado College State of the Rockies, Wyoming registered voters (n=406), Jan 2-18, 2026
issue_poll.note: Combined three Wyoming polls. No 2026 all-voter Wyoming poll with a general ranked issue list was found. Ranks 1-5 are the Cygnal most-important-issue order (closest to Election Day; only the top five were published; cost of living 21%+, taxes/spending 14%, immigration 13%, jobs/economy 11%, public lands 11% - the last two tied). Ranks 6-9 are the highest remaining items from the NCHT poll (https://collectivehealthtrust.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/NBS_Report_041726-1.pdf): health care cost 81% / availability 62% merged, housing cost 67%, suicide 64% / mental health 63% merged, drug and alcohol use 54%. NCHT's 'rising cost of living' (74%) and 'lack of well-paid jobs' (61%) fold into ranks 1 and 4. Excluded as not testable by a Senate vote: state budget (54%, set by the Wyoming Legislature), young residents/families leaving the state (48%/44%), social isolation (38%). Rank 10, wildfire (51% extremely/very serious), comes from State of the Rockies (https://www.coloradocollege.edu/other/stateoftherockies/conservationinthewest/2026-poll-data/2026-state-of-the-rockies%20deck%20FINAL.pdf), which uses the same 'extremely/very serious problem' wording; it outranks NCHT's next testable items (immigration 34%, hunger 30%).

issues.detail: Cut federal red tape to improve affordability; reduce federal spending; no specific measure
Reduce federal spending; no target, cap or named bill
Keep border security funded; prioritize deporting criminal noncitizens; merit-based legal immigration (education, skills, assimilation); remove illegal/unqualified truck drivers
Regulatory reform and permitting modernization; protect legacy energy industries and small businesses; empower states
Roll back the Roadless Rule on Wyoming national forests; multiple-use and sustained-yield management with local input
Back existing Rural Health Transformation Program; Wyoming joining a larger insurance marketplace; review drug pricing rules
Points to enacted 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (construction, permitting, financing); no new measure
Pass the Fix Our Forests Act (S.1462, pending in Senate)

plan_caveats: Ranks 1-5 come from a poll of Republican primary voters only (about 74% of Wyoming registrants are Republican), sponsored by a public-lands advocacy campaign; only its top five issues were published, via WyoFile, not the poll itself.

Issue list stitches together three polls with different questions (most important issue vs. 'serious problem'); the order between the Cygnal block and the NCHT/State of the Rockies block is a judgment call.

Hageman published no 2026 issue pages that could be found (campaign site hagemanforwyoming.com could not be fetched), skipped the general-election PBS debates, and did not answer Ballotpedia's survey; positions come from WyoFile/JH News&Guide questionnaires, the July 8 Casper forum and press coverage.

Public lands rated Concrete on the Roadless Rule rollback, reported by Wyoming Public Media as something she is 'working to' do during the campaign; much of her public-lands record (Utah land case, roadless-area bill) is House record, not a campaign promise, and was not counted.
Wildfire rated Concrete because she cited the pending Fix Our Forests Act at a campaign forum as a measure she backs; she did not explicitly pledge a Senate vote for it.
Grizzly bear delisting and coal leasing pushes were House activity, not 2026 campaign statements, so they were not counted.
Primary debate (Aug 13, 2026, Wyoming PBS) video was not transcribed; it may contain additional positions.
